body.mechanism_of_action: Competitively inhibits intestinal alpha-glucosidases (maltase, sucrase, glucoamylase), delaying carbohydrate digestion and reducing postprandial glucose absorption

Mucolytic: cleaves disulphide bonds in mucus glycoproteins, reducing mucus viscosity. Antioxidant: precursor of glutathione (GSH), replenishing intracellular GSH stores. In paracetamol overdose, provides sulphydryl groups to conjugate NAPQI.

Selectively phosphorylated by viral thymidine kinase (TK) in infected cells, then converted to acyclovir triphosphate which inhibits viral DNA polymerase and terminates DNA chain elongation. Minimal effect on uninfected host cells.

body.black_box_warning: Serious infections (TB, invasive fungal infections, opportunistic infections). Malignancy risk including lymphoma. Screen for latent TB before initiation.
body.mechanism_of_action: Fully human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds to TNF-alpha with high affinity, preventing its interaction with p55 and p75 TNF receptors. Reduces inflammatory cytokine cascade, leukocyte migration, and angiogenesis.

Potent agonist at alpha-1 (vasoconstriction), alpha-2, beta-1 (inotropy, chronotropy), and beta-2 (bronchodilation, vasodilation) adrenergic receptors. In anaphylaxis: reverses vasodilation, reduces oedema, bronchodilates, and augments cardiac output.

Binds to hydroxyapatite in bone, is internalised by osteoclasts during resorption, and inhibits farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase (mevalonate pathway). This disrupts osteoclast cytoskeleton, signalling, and induces osteoclast apoptosis, reducing bone resorption.

Synthetic 1-alpha-hydroxylated vitamin D3 that requires only hepatic 25-hydroxylation (not renal 1-alpha-hydroxylation) to become active 1,25(OH)2D3 (calcitriol). Bypasses the defective renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase in CKD. Increases intestinal calcium and phosphate absorption, promotes bone mineralisation, and suppresses PTH secretion.
Inhibits xanthine oxidase, blocking the conversion of hypoxanthine to xanthine and xanthine to uric acid. Active metabolite oxypurinol also inhibits xanthine oxidase with a longer half-life.

body.black_box_warning: Risk of fatal intracranial haemorrhage (~6% symptomatic ICH). Strict eligibility criteria must be met. Must be administered within 4.5 hours of symptom onset. Requires neuroimaging to exclude haemorrhage before administration.
body.mechanism_of_action: Recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rt-PA). Binds to fibrin in a thrombus and converts entrapped plasminogen to plasmin, which degrades the fibrin matrix of the clot. Relatively fibrin-selective at therapeutic doses.

Aminophylline is 80% theophylline by weight (plus ethylenediamine for solubility). Acts as a non-selective PDE inhibitor and adenosine receptor antagonist — same mechanism as theophylline but allows IV administration.

body.black_box_warning: Pulmonary toxicity (potentially fatal), hepatotoxicity, and proarrhythmia. Use only for life-threatening arrhythmias when other agents are ineffective or contraindicated.
body.mechanism_of_action: Blocks potassium channels (class III), sodium channels (class I), calcium channels (class IV), and beta-adrenergic receptors (class II). Also has anti-thyroid properties due to high iodine content (37% by weight). Prolongs action potential duration and effective refractory period in all cardiac tissues.

Inhibits L-type calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle, causing peripheral arterial vasodilation and reduced afterload. No significant effect on cardiac conduction or myocardial contractility at therapeutic doses.
Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), preventing cross-linking of peptidoglycan chains. Bactericidal against susceptible organisms.
Amoxicillin inhibits cell wall synthesis via PBP binding. Clavulanate irreversibly inhibits class A beta-lactamases (TEM, SHV), restoring amoxicillin activity against resistant organisms.

body.black_box_warning: Different amphotericin B formulations are NOT interchangeable — dose and toxicity profiles differ. Verify product before administration.
body.mechanism_of_action: Binds to ergosterol in the fungal cell membrane, forming pores that cause leakage of intracellular contents and cell death. Liposomal encapsulation preferentially targets fungal cell membranes, reducing binding to human cholesterol and thus reducing nephrotoxicity.

Synthetic human angiotensin II that binds AT1 receptors on vascular smooth muscle causing vasoconstriction; also stimulates aldosterone release increasing sodium reabsorption and intravascular volume; acts synergistically with catecholamines
Non-competitive inhibitor of 1,3-beta-D-glucan synthase, disrupting fungal cell wall synthesis; fungicidal against Candida spp.
Directly and selectively inhibits free and clot-bound Factor Xa, blocking thrombin generation. Does not require antithrombin III as a cofactor.

body.pregnancy_category: Category D (third trimester); Category C (first/second trimester)
body.mechanism_of_action: Irreversibly acetylates cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1), blocking thromboxane A2 (TXA2) synthesis in platelets for their entire lifespan (7-10 days). At higher doses, also inhibits COX-2 and prostaglandin synthesis.

Selective beta-1 adrenergic receptor antagonist. Reduces heart rate, cardiac output, and myocardial oxygen demand. Hydrophilic — does not readily cross the blood-brain barrier, resulting in fewer CNS side effects.
Competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme in cholesterol biosynthesis in the liver. Upregulates hepatic LDL receptors, increasing LDL-C clearance from plasma.

Binds to 50S ribosomal subunit, inhibiting mRNA-directed protein synthesis. Bacteriostatic at usual concentrations; may be bactericidal at high tissue concentrations. Concentrates in phagocytes and is delivered to sites of infection.

body.black_box_warning: Serious infections, malignancy, thrombosis, and cardiovascular events. Not recommended in patients >50 years with CV risk factors due to increased risk of major adverse CV events and malignancies compared to TNF inhibitors.
body.pregnancy_category: Avoid — fetal harm demonstrated in animal studies; use effective contraception
body.mechanism_of_action: Selective, reversible inhibitor of JAK1 and JAK2, blocking cytokine signaling (IL-6, IFN-γ, GM-CSF) via STAT pathway suppression, reducing inflammatory gene transcription
Prodrug converted to active metabolite beclometasone-17-monopropionate (17-BMP) by lung esterases. Binds glucocorticoid receptors to suppress airway inflammation.

body.black_box_warning: Serious infections and mortality; serious neuropsychiatric events including depression and suicidality reported
body.mechanism_of_action: Fully human IgG1λ monoclonal antibody that binds soluble BLyS (B-lymphocyte stimulator/BAFF), preventing it from binding to receptors on B cells, thereby inhibiting B-cell survival, differentiation, and immunoglobulin production in SLE

body.pregnancy_category: No adequate human data; use only if benefit outweighs risk
body.mechanism_of_action: Humanized afucosylated IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody that binds to IL-5 receptor alpha (IL-5Rα) on eosinophils and basophils, blocking IL-5 signaling and inducing enhanced antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC) via NK cells, leading to rapid and near-complete eosinophil depletion

body.black_box_warning: Abrupt discontinuation in ischemic heart disease may precipitate angina, MI, or ventricular arrhythmias. Taper dose gradually over 1–2 weeks.
body.mechanism_of_action: Selective beta-1 adrenergic receptor antagonist; reduces heart rate, myocardial contractility, and cardiac output; lowers blood pressure; also reduces intraocular pressure by decreasing aqueous humor production when used topically.

body.pregnancy_category: Category D (third trimester due to salicylate); Category C (first/second trimester)
body.mechanism_of_action: Multi-modal: bismuth has direct antimicrobial activity against H. pylori, forms a protective coating over ulcerated mucosa, stimulates bicarbonate and prostaglandin secretion. The salicylate component has antisecretory and anti-inflammatory effects in the GI mucosa.

Highly selective beta-1 adrenergic receptor antagonist. Reduces heart rate, cardiac output, and myocardial oxygen demand. Decreases renin secretion. Has the highest beta-1 selectivity among beta-blockers.

Reversibly inhibits the 26S proteasome chymotrypsin-like activity, blocking ubiquitin-proteasome pathway degradation of regulatory proteins, inducing cell cycle arrest and apoptosis in malignant cells
High-affinity selective ligand for synaptic vesicle protein 2A (SV2A), modulating neurotransmitter release and reducing neuronal hyperexcitability

Binds intracellular glucocorticoid receptors, translocating to the nucleus to suppress transcription of pro-inflammatory genes (cytokines, chemokines, adhesion molecules). Reduces airway inflammation, oedema, and mucus hypersecretion.

Binds glucocorticoid receptors with high affinity; exerts local anti-inflammatory effects in the gut mucosa with extensive first-pass hepatic metabolism (~90%), minimizing systemic corticosteroid effects

body.black_box_warning: Increased risk of suicidal thinking and behavior in children, adolescents, and young adults (18-24 years) with major depressive disorder and other psychiatric disorders. Monitor closely for worsening and emergence of suicidal thoughts.
body.mechanism_of_action: Inhibits neuronal reuptake of dopamine and norepinephrine (NDRI); weak nicotinic acetylcholine receptor antagonist. Does not inhibit MAO or serotonin reuptake.

body.pregnancy_category: Not classified — considered safe for external use
body.mechanism_of_action: Zinc oxide component provides mild astringent and antiseptic action. Evaporation of the aqueous phase produces a cooling effect on the skin, soothing pruritus. Iron oxide (ferric oxide) imparts the characteristic pink colour.

Calcium binds dietary phosphate in the GI tract to form insoluble calcium phosphate, which is excreted in faeces. Calcium acetate has greater phosphate-binding capacity per amount of calcium absorbed compared to calcium carbonate, resulting in less calcium absorption.

Provides elemental calcium (40% by weight) for bone mineralisation, neuromuscular function, and intracellular signalling. As a phosphate binder in CKD: calcium binds dietary phosphate in the gut to form insoluble calcium-phosphate complexes, reducing phosphate absorption.

body.black_box_warning: Lower limb amputation risk (primarily toe/metatarsal); weigh benefits vs risks in patients with peripheral vascular disease or neuropathy
body.mechanism_of_action: Selectively inhibits sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) in proximal renal tubule, reducing glucose reabsorption and lowering renal threshold for glucose, resulting in urinary glucose excretion independent of insulin
Reversible, direct-acting P2Y12 receptor antagonist; blocks ADP-induced platelet activation and aggregation without requiring hepatic conversion to an active metabolite

body.black_box_warning: Serious dermatological reactions (SJS/TEN) — strongly associated with HLA-B*1502 allele (prevalent in Southeast/East Asian populations). Screen before initiating in at-risk ethnicities. Also risk of aplastic anaemia and agranulocytosis.
body.mechanism_of_action: Blocks voltage-gated sodium channels in their inactivated state, stabilising neuronal membranes. Reduces repetitive firing of action potentials. Also modulates L-type calcium channels.

body.pregnancy_category: Category D (teratogenic — aplasia cutis, choanal atresia)
body.mechanism_of_action: Prodrug rapidly converted to methimazole. Inhibits thyroid peroxidase (TPO), blocking iodine organification and coupling of iodotyrosines, thereby reducing T3 and T4 synthesis. Does not block release of preformed hormone.

Regulates mucus production by normalising the ratio of sialomucins to fucomucins in bronchial secretions. Reduces mucus viscosity and improves mucociliary clearance without directly breaking disulphide bonds (unlike acetylcysteine).

body.drug_class: Non-selective beta-blocker with alpha-1 blocking activity
body.mechanism_of_action: Non-selective beta-1 and beta-2 adrenergic receptor antagonist with additional alpha-1 receptor blockade causing vasodilation. Possesses antioxidant properties. Reduces preload and afterload in addition to heart rate reduction.

body.black_box_warning: Higher all-cause mortality observed in CREDIBLE-CR trial vs best available therapy in carbapenem-resistant gram-negative infections; cause not established.
body.pregnancy_category: No adequate human data; animal studies show no teratogenicity
body.mechanism_of_action: Binds ferric iron via catechol siderophore moiety to hijack bacterial iron-uptake transporters, enabling active transport across outer membrane; inhibits penicillin-binding proteins (PBP1b, PBP3) disrupting cell wall synthesis. Stable against most beta-lactamases including carbapenemases (KPC, MBL, OXA).

Ceftazidime inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs); avibactam is a non-beta-lactam beta-lactamase inhibitor that reversibly inhibits class A (KPC), class C (AmpC), and some class D (OXA-48) beta-lactamases, restoring ceftazidime activity against resistant organisms

body.black_box_warning: Neonates: Do NOT co-administer with calcium-containing IV solutions or products — fatal ceftriaxone-calcium precipitates have occurred in neonatal lungs and kidneys.
body.mechanism_of_action: Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to PBPs (especially PBP3), disrupting peptidoglycan cross-linking. Bactericidal with broad Gram-negative coverage and stability against many beta-lactamases.

Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to PBPs. Stable against many beta-lactamases produced by Gram-negatives. Better Gram-negative coverage than first-gen cephalosporins while retaining Gram-positive activity.

Selective peripheral H1 receptor antagonist with minimal blood-brain barrier penetration. Active carboxylic acid metabolite of hydroxyzine. Inhibits histamine-mediated early-phase allergic response and eosinophil chemotaxis in late-phase.

Competitive antagonist at histamine H1 receptors with additional anticholinergic and mild sedative properties. Crosses the blood-brain barrier. Reduces histamine-mediated vasodilation, increased permeability, and pruritus.

body.drug_class: Vitamin D supplement / Secosteroid hormone precursor
body.pregnancy_category: Category A (at recommended doses); Category D at excessive doses
body.mechanism_of_action: Cholecalciferol (D3) is hydroxylated in the liver to 25-hydroxyvitamin D (calcidiol), then in the kidney to 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D (calcitriol, active form). Calcitriol binds VDR nuclear receptors to increase intestinal calcium and phosphate absorption, promote bone mineralisation, and modulate immune function.

Binds to cyclophilin, forming a complex that inhibits calcineurin phosphatase. This prevents dephosphorylation of NFAT, blocking IL-2 transcription and T-cell activation. Predominantly inhibits T-helper cell function.

Allosteric activator of calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR) on parathyroid chief cells; increases receptor sensitivity to extracellular calcium, suppressing PTH secretion and reducing serum calcium and phosphorus

body.black_box_warning: FDA Black Box Warning: Fluoroquinolones are associated with disabling and potentially irreversible serious adverse reactions including tendinitis/tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, and CNS effects. Also associated with aortic aneurysm/dissection. Reserve for conditions with no alternative treatment options.
body.mechanism_of_action: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV, preventing DNA supercoiling, replication, transcription, and repair. Bactericidal with concentration-dependent killing.

body.black_box_warning: Should be administered only by personnel skilled in airway management and respiratory support.
body.mechanism_of_action: Competitive antagonist at nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, preventing acetylcholine-mediated depolarization and causing skeletal muscle paralysis.

Binds to 50S ribosomal subunit, inhibiting translocation of aminoacyl transfer-RNA and protein synthesis. Bacteriostatic; active metabolite (14-OH-clarithromycin) provides synergistic activity against H. influenzae.

body.black_box_warning: Rebound hypertension may occur upon abrupt discontinuation; do not use in patients with allergies to soybeans, soy products, eggs, or egg products due to lipid emulsion formulation.
body.mechanism_of_action: Selective L-type calcium channel blocker acting on vascular smooth muscle, causing arteriolar vasodilation and reduction in systemic vascular resistance without affecting cardiac contractility or venous capacitance.

Binds to the 50S ribosomal subunit (23S rRNA), inhibiting peptide bond formation and bacterial protein synthesis. Bacteriostatic; may be bactericidal at high concentrations against susceptible organisms.

Prodrug that requires hepatic CYP2C19-mediated bioactivation. Active metabolite irreversibly binds the P2Y12 ADP receptor on platelets, inhibiting ADP-mediated platelet activation and aggregation for the platelet's lifespan.

body.black_box_warning: Severe neutropenia/agranulocytosis (1-2%): mandatory FBC monitoring. Myocarditis and cardiomyopathy. Seizures (dose-related). Severe orthostatic hypotension with syncope and respiratory/cardiac arrest.
body.mechanism_of_action: Antagonist at D1, D2, D3, D4 (high D4 affinity), 5-HT2A, 5-HT2C, muscarinic M1/M4, histamine H1, and alpha-1 adrenergic receptors. Unique efficacy in treatment-resistant schizophrenia linked to D4/5-HT2A ratio and glutamate modulation.

body.black_box_warning: CYP2D6 ultra-rapid metabolisers convert codeine to morphine at greatly increased rates, risking fatal respiratory depression — particularly dangerous in children, post-tonsillectomy, and breastfeeding mothers.
body.mechanism_of_action: Pro-drug requiring hepatic CYP2D6-mediated O-demethylation to morphine (active metabolite), which acts as a mu-opioid receptor agonist. Approximately 5-10% of codeine is converted to morphine in extensive metabolisers. Also has direct antitussive activity in the medulla.

Binds tubulin, inhibiting microtubule polymerisation. Disrupts neutrophil migration, phagocytosis, and NLRP3 inflammasome activation, reducing IL-1-beta production. Highly selective for gouty inflammation.

body.black_box_warning: Nephrotoxicity and neurotoxicity have been reported; use with caution in patients with renal impairment. Reduce dose as appropriate.
body.mechanism_of_action: Disrupts the integrity of the bacterial outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria by competitively displacing divalent cations (Ca2+, Mg2+) from phospholipid binding sites on lipopolysaccharide (LPS), increasing membrane permeability and causing cell death

body.black_box_warning: Nephrotoxicity and neurotoxicity: Colistimethate sodium (CMS) can cause serious nephrotoxicity and neurotoxicity. Nephrotoxicity is dose-dependent and may be irreversible. Neurotoxicity may manifest as respiratory muscle paralysis leading to apnea. Risk increases with concomitant use of nephrotoxic agents, aminoglycosides, or neuromuscular blocking agents. Use with extreme caution in patients with renal impairment; dose adjustment is mandatory.
body.pregnancy_category: FDA Category C; TGA Category B3 — animal studies show some fetal risk; use only if potential benefit justifies risk. Colistin crosses the placenta; neonatal nephrotoxicity reported.
body.mechanism_of_action: Colistin is a cationic polypeptide antibiotic that acts as a detergent on bacterial cell membranes. It binds electrostatically to the anionic lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and phospholipids in the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria, displacing divalent cations (Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺) that stabilize the outer membrane. This destabilizes and disrupts the outer and inner bacterial cell membranes, causing increased membrane permeability, leakage of intracellular contents, and ultimately cell death. It is concentration-dependent and bactericidal. Activity is primarily against Gram-negative organisms including Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Klebsiella pneumoniae (including carbapenem-resistant strains). Note: Colistin is administered as an inactive prodrug, colistimethate sodium (CMS), which is hydrolyzed in vivo to active colistin.
Blocks histamine H1 receptors and muscarinic receptors in the vomiting centre and vestibular nuclei, suppressing nausea and vomiting particularly of vestibular and opioid-induced origin.

body.pregnancy_category: Category C — embryotoxic in animal studies; avoid in pregnancy
body.mechanism_of_action: Prodrug hydrolysed to dabigatran, which directly and reversibly binds to the active site of thrombin (factor IIa), inhibiting both free and clot-bound thrombin. Prevents fibrin formation and thrombin-mediated platelet activation.

Selectively inhibits SGLT2 in the proximal renal tubule, reducing glucose reabsorption and promoting glycosuria. Produces osmotic diuresis, natriuresis, and reduces intraglomerular pressure independent of insulin.

body.black_box_warning: Eosinophilic pneumonia and other pulmonary eosinophilic conditions have been reported. Daptomycin is not indicated for the treatment of pneumonia due to inactivation by pulmonary surfactant.
body.pregnancy_category: B – Animal reproduction studies have failed to demonstrate a risk to the fetus. No adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women exist. Use only if clearly needed.
body.mechanism_of_action: Daptomycin is a cyclic lipopeptide antibiotic that binds in a calcium-dependent manner to phosphatidylglycerol in the bacterial cytoplasmic membrane of gram-positive organisms. This binding causes rapid membrane depolarization, leading to loss of membrane potential, inhibition of DNA, RNA, and protein synthesis, and ultimately bacterial cell death. It is bactericidal in a concentration-dependent manner. Daptomycin does not penetrate the cell wall; its mechanism is distinct from beta-lactams, glycopeptides, and other antibiotics.

body.black_box_warning: Increased risk of death, myocardial infarction, stroke, and tumour progression when targeting Hb >130 g/L. Use lowest dose to avoid RBC transfusion.
body.mechanism_of_action: Hyperglycosylated analogue of erythropoietin with longer half-life. Binds to erythropoietin receptors on erythroid progenitor cells in bone marrow, stimulating proliferation, differentiation, and survival of red blood cell precursors.

Selective V2-receptor agonist on renal collecting duct principal cells — inserts aquaporin-2 channels in the apical membrane, promoting free water reabsorption. Also releases VWF and factor VIII from endothelial stores (via V2 receptors on endothelium). Minimal V1a activity (no vasopressor effect at therapeutic doses).

Potent synthetic glucocorticoid with 25-30x the anti-inflammatory potency of hydrocortisone and negligible mineralocorticoid activity. Binds glucocorticoid receptors, suppressing NF-κB and pro-inflammatory gene transcription. Crosses the blood-brain barrier effectively. Crosses the placenta (unlike prednisolone, which is inactivated by placental 11-beta-HSD2) — hence used for fetal lung maturation.

Highly selective alpha-2 adrenoreceptor agonist in the locus coeruleus, producing dose-dependent sedation, anxiolysis, and analgesia without significant respiratory depression. Mimics natural sleep pathways (NREM stage 2-like sedation).

Binds to the benzodiazepine site on GABA-A receptors (at the alpha/gamma subunit interface), enhancing the frequency of chloride channel opening in response to GABA. This increases inhibitory neurotransmission. Also has muscle relaxant properties via spinal cord GABA-A receptors.

Inhibits Na+/K+-ATPase in myocardial cells, increasing intracellular Na+ which reduces Ca2+ extrusion via NCX, raising intracellular Ca2+ and enhancing contractility (positive inotropy). Increases vagal tone to the AV node (negative dromotropy), slowing ventricular rate in AF.

Blocks L-type calcium channels in cardiac and vascular smooth muscle. Reduces heart rate (negative chronotropy), slows AV nodal conduction (negative dromotropy), and causes coronary/peripheral vasodilation. Less negative inotropy than verapamil.
Anionic surfactant that lowers surface tension at the oil-water interface of stool, allowing water and fat to penetrate the faecal mass. Also has mild stimulant effect on colonic mucosal secretion.

body.black_box_warning: Risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias including QT prolongation, torsades de pointes, and sudden cardiac death. Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration.
body.mechanism_of_action: Blocks dopamine D2 receptors in the chemoreceptor trigger zone (antiemetic) and in the upper GI tract (prokinetic), enhancing gastric motility and accelerating gastric emptying without crossing the blood-brain barrier significantly.

body.pregnancy_category: C – Animal studies have shown adverse effects on the fetus; no adequate and well-controlled studies in humans. Use only if potential benefit justifies potential risk to the fetus.
body.mechanism_of_action: Donepezil is a reversible, competitive inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase (AChE), the enzyme responsible for the hydrolysis of acetylcholine in the synaptic cleft. By inhibiting AChE, donepezil increases the concentration and duration of action of acetylcholine at cholinergic synapses in the cerebral cortex and hippocampus. This enhancement of cholinergic neurotransmission partially compensates for the loss of functioning cholinergic neurons characteristic of Alzheimer's disease. Donepezil is approximately 1000-fold more selective for AChE than for butyrylcholinesterase (BuChE), minimizing peripheral cholinergic side effects. It also has modest effects on nicotinic acetylcholine receptors and may provide some neuroprotection through reduction of beta-amyloid-induced apoptosis.

Dose-dependent receptor activation: low dose (1-5 mcg/kg/min) — D1/D2 dopaminergic receptors (renal/mesenteric vasodilation); moderate dose (5-10 mcg/kg/min) — beta-1 (inotropy, chronotropy); high dose (>10 mcg/kg/min) — alpha-1 (vasoconstriction).

Stimulates peripheral chemoreceptors (carotid body) at low doses and central medullary respiratory centres at higher doses, increasing tidal volume and respiratory rate. Also has mild CNS-stimulant properties.

Doxazosin is a selective, competitive antagonist of post-synaptic alpha-1 adrenoceptors (alpha-1A, alpha-1B, and alpha-1D subtypes), which are Gq/11 protein-coupled receptors. Blockade of vascular alpha-1 adrenoceptors prevents norepinephrine-mediated vasoconstriction, leading to relaxation of both arterial and venous smooth muscle and a reduction in peripheral vascular resistance, thereby lowering blood pressure. In benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), selective blockade of alpha-1A adrenoceptors in the prostate stroma, bladder neck, and urethra reduces smooth muscle tone, relieving bladder outlet obstruction and improving urinary flow. Alpha-1D receptor blockade in the bladder detrusor may additionally reduce irritative urinary symptoms. Unlike non-selective alpha blockers, doxazosin does not significantly block alpha-2 adrenoceptors, minimizing reflex tachycardia. The drug does not cause receptor downregulation with chronic use.

Binds to 30S ribosomal subunit, inhibiting binding of aminoacyl-tRNA to the mRNA-ribosome complex. Bacteriostatic. Also has anti-inflammatory properties (inhibits MMPs, cytokines) — basis for use in acne and periodontitis.

body.black_box_warning: Contraindicated in permanent atrial fibrillation and symptomatic heart failure with recent decompensation or NYHA Class IV; doubles mortality, stroke, and HF hospitalization in these patients (PALLAS trial).
body.mechanism_of_action: Multichannel blocker with properties of all four Vaughan-Williams classes: blocks IKr, IKs, INa, ICa-L, and beta-adrenergic receptors. Unlike amiodarone, lacks iodine moiety reducing thyroid/pulmonary toxicity.

body.black_box_warning: Dulaglutide causes dose-dependent and treatment-duration-dependent thyroid C-cell tumors in rats. It is unknown whether dulaglutide causes thyroid C-cell tumors, including medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), in humans. Dulaglutide is contraindicated in patients with a personal or family history of MTC or in patients with Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2).
body.pregnancy_category: FDA: Discontinue when pregnancy recognized; limited human data — animal studies show adverse fetal effects (TGA: Category C equivalent). Avoid use in pregnancy.
body.mechanism_of_action: Dulaglutide is a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist consisting of two GLP-1 analogue sequences covalently linked to a modified human IgG4 Fc fragment. It binds and activates GLP-1 receptors on pancreatic beta cells, stimulating glucose-dependent insulin secretion and suppressing glucagon release from alpha cells. It also slows gastric emptying, reduces appetite via central hypothalamic pathways, and promotes satiety. Because its insulinotropic effects are glucose-dependent, the risk of hypoglycemia is low when used as monotherapy. The Fc linkage extends the half-life to approximately 5 days, enabling once-weekly dosing.

body.black_box_warning: Increased risk of suicidal thinking and behavior in children, adolescents, and young adults (18–24 years) with MDD and other psychiatric disorders during initial treatment.
body.mechanism_of_action: Inhibits reuptake of serotonin (5-HT) and norepinephrine (NE) at presynaptic terminals, increasing their synaptic availability; no significant affinity for dopaminergic, histaminergic, or muscarinic receptors.

body.pregnancy_category: No FDA letter category; monoclonal antibodies cross placenta in third trimester — use only if benefit outweighs risk
body.mechanism_of_action: Fully human IgG4 monoclonal antibody that binds IL-4Rα subunit, blocking signaling of both IL-4 and IL-13 — key Th2 cytokines driving type 2 inflammation in atopic dermatitis, asthma, and CRSwNP

body.black_box_warning: Premature discontinuation of edoxaban increases the risk of ischemic events. If anticoagulation with edoxaban must be discontinued for a reason other than pathological bleeding, consider coverage with another anticoagulant. Edoxaban is not recommended in patients with CrCl >95 mL/min for non-valvular atrial fibrillation due to increased risk of ischemic stroke compared to warfarin.
body.pregnancy_category: Not formally categorised (FDA 2015 labelling system); animal studies show fetal harm — use only if clearly necessary; avoid if possible (similar to TGA Category C/D risk profile)
body.mechanism_of_action: Edoxaban is a highly selective, direct, reversible inhibitor of factor Xa (fXa), the final common enzyme in the intrinsic and extrinsic coagulation cascades responsible for converting prothrombin to thrombin. By binding directly to the active site of both free fXa and fXa within the prothrombinase complex, edoxaban inhibits thrombin generation and subsequent fibrin clot formation without requiring antithrombin III as a cofactor. It does not directly inhibit thrombin (factor IIa) and has no effect on platelet aggregation. Inhibition of fXa reduces both arterial and venous thrombosis while producing a more predictable anticoagulant response than vitamin K antagonists.

Selectively inhibits sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) in the proximal tubule, reducing renal glucose reabsorption and causing glycosuria (80-90 g/day). Provides osmotic diuresis, natriuresis, and reduces intraglomerular pressure.

body.black_box_warning: Drugs that act on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing foetus. Discontinue as soon as pregnancy is detected.
body.mechanism_of_action: Prodrug hydrolysed in the liver to enalaprilat, which inhibits ACE. Prevents conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II, reduces aldosterone secretion, and increases bradykinin. Enalaprilat is the only IV ACE inhibitor available.

Binds antithrombin III, potentiating its inhibition of Factor Xa (primary) and Factor IIa (thrombin, to a lesser extent). Anti-Xa to anti-IIa ratio approximately 3.8:1, providing more predictable anticoagulation than unfractionated heparin.

body.pregnancy_category: Category B (animal data) — insufficient human data
body.mechanism_of_action: Selectively blocks mineralocorticoid (aldosterone) receptors with minimal affinity for androgen, progesterone, and glucocorticoid receptors — avoids gynaecomastia seen with spironolactone. Reduces aldosterone-mediated sodium retention, myocardial fibrosis, and vascular remodelling.
Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), disrupting peptidoglycan cross-linking; bactericidal with time-dependent killing

body.black_box_warning: Suicidality: Increased risk of suicidal thinking and behaviour in children, adolescents, and young adults (18-24 years).
body.mechanism_of_action: S-enantiomer of citalopram. Highly selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SERT). Binds to both the primary (orthosteric) and allosteric sites on SERT, enhancing potency and selectivity. Minimal activity at other receptors.

Selective beta-1 adrenergic receptor antagonist with rapid onset and ultra-short duration. Reduces heart rate, contractility, and AV conduction. No intrinsic sympathomimetic or membrane-stabilising activity.

S-isomer of omeprazole. Irreversibly inhibits the H+/K+-ATPase proton pump on the parietal cell apical membrane, blocking the final common pathway of gastric acid secretion. Reduces basal and stimulated acid output by >90%.

body.drug_class: Anti-TNF fusion protein (TNF receptor p75-Fc fusion protein)
body.black_box_warning: Serious infections (bacterial, fungal, viral, opportunistic including TB) and malignancies (lymphoma and other cancers, including in children and adolescents) have been reported.
body.mechanism_of_action: Dimeric fusion protein consisting of human TNF receptor p75 linked to Fc portion of IgG1. Competitively binds soluble and membrane-bound TNF-alpha and TNF-beta (lymphotoxin-alpha), preventing interaction with cell surface TNF receptors, thereby reducing pro-inflammatory cytokine cascade.
Inhibits arabinosyl transferase (EmbB), blocking arabinogalactan synthesis and mycobacterial cell wall assembly. Bacteriostatic at standard doses.
Selectively inhibits xanthine oxidase (both oxidised and reduced forms), reducing uric acid production. Non-purine structure — does not affect other enzymes in purine/pyrimidine metabolism.

Provides elemental iron (ferrous form, Fe2+) for absorption in the duodenum and proximal jejunum via divalent metal transporter 1 (DMT1). Iron is incorporated into haemoglobin, myoglobin, and iron-containing enzymes.
Selective peripheral H1-receptor inverse agonist. Active metabolite of terfenadine without cardiac ion channel effects — does not prolong QTc.

Recombinant human G-CSF (non-glycosylated, produced in E. coli). Binds to G-CSF receptors on neutrophil precursors, stimulating proliferation, differentiation, and functional activation of neutrophils. Also mobilises haematopoietic stem cells from bone marrow into peripheral blood.

body.pregnancy_category: N/A (FDA labeling post-2015; use not recommended in pregnancy due to potential fetal harm based on mechanism; contraindicated in pregnancy per some guidelines)
body.mechanism_of_action: Finerenone is a selective, non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA) that binds with high affinity and selectivity to the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR), blocking the binding of aldosterone and other MR-activating factors such as cortisol. Unlike steroidal MRAs (spironolactone, eplerenone), finerenone has a bulkier side chain that induces a distinct receptor conformation, preventing recruitment of coactivators and resulting in full antagonism without partial agonist activity. This leads to reduced MR-mediated transcription of pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic genes (including PAI-1, TGF-β, NF-κB pathway targets, and connective tissue growth factor). In the kidneys and heart, excess MR activation — driven by aldosterone and non-aldosterone ligands in the setting of cardiorenal disease and diabetes — contributes to inflammation, fibrosis, oxidative stress, and endothelial dysfunction. Finerenone's blockade attenuates these processes, reducing glomerular inflammation, tubular injury, cardiac fibrosis, and vascular damage. Its non-steroidal structure also confers higher selectivity for MR over androgen, progesterone, and glucocorticoid receptors compared to spironolactone, minimizing off-target hormonal side effects. Finerenone distributes more equally between cardiac and renal tissues compared to eplerenone, potentially providing more balanced organ protection.

body.pregnancy_category: Category D (high dose / chronic); single 150 mg likely safe
body.mechanism_of_action: Inhibits fungal cytochrome P450 14α-demethylase (CYP51), blocking conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol. Depletes ergosterol in fungal cell membrane, increasing permeability. Fungistatic against Candida; fungicidal against Cryptococcus at higher doses.

Potent synthetic mineralocorticoid that acts on renal distal tubule mineralocorticoid receptors — promotes sodium and water reabsorption and potassium/hydrogen excretion. Has 10x the mineralocorticoid potency of hydrocortisone with some residual glucocorticoid activity.

Potent glucocorticoid receptor agonist with high topical anti-inflammatory activity. Suppresses inflammatory gene transcription, reduces eosinophilic infiltration, and decreases airway hyperresponsiveness.

Converted to tetrahydrofolate (THF) via dihydrofolate reductase, serving as a one-carbon carrier in nucleotide synthesis (thymidylate and purine biosynthesis). Essential for DNA synthesis and cell division, particularly in rapidly dividing cells (bone marrow, fetal tissues).

body.pregnancy_category: Category B — limited human data; used when heparin contraindicated (e.g. HIT in pregnancy)
body.mechanism_of_action: Synthetic analogue of the antithrombin-binding pentasaccharide sequence of heparin. Selectively binds antithrombin III, catalysing factor Xa inhibition with >300-fold increased potency. Does NOT inhibit thrombin (IIa) and does NOT bind to PF4 — hence no HIT.

body.black_box_warning: LABAs increase the risk of asthma-related death. Use only with a concomitant ICS — NEVER as monotherapy in asthma.
body.mechanism_of_action: Full beta-2 agonist with rapid onset and 12-hour duration. Moderately lipophilic — rapidly penetrates cell membrane to reach receptor while maintaining prolonged action via depot effect in lipid membrane.

Inhibits sodium-potassium-2 chloride (Na-K-2Cl) co-transporter in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle, preventing reabsorption of sodium, potassium, and chloride, resulting in profound diuresis.

body.black_box_warning: Nephrotoxicity and irreversible ototoxicity (vestibular and cochlear). Neuromuscular blockade and respiratory paralysis reported.
body.mechanism_of_action: Binds irreversibly to the 30S ribosomal subunit, causing misreading of mRNA and production of aberrant proteins. Bactericidal with concentration-dependent killing and prolonged post-antibiotic effect.
Binds to SUR1 subunit of ATP-sensitive potassium channels on pancreatic beta cells, causing depolarisation and insulin secretion. Also has extrapancreatic effects including reduced platelet adhesion.

Binds glucagon receptors on hepatocytes, activating adenylyl cyclase and increasing cAMP, which stimulates glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, raising blood glucose. Also has positive inotropic and chronotropic effects on the heart via a non-beta-adrenergic mechanism (direct cAMP-mediated).

body.drug_class: Hypertonic glucose solution (caloric agent / hypoglycaemia treatment)
body.mechanism_of_action: Provides exogenous glucose (500 mg/mL) for immediate cellular energy substrate. In hypoglycaemia, rapidly restores blood glucose levels. Each 50 mL ampoule delivers 25 g of glucose. Stimulates endogenous insulin release in non-diabetic patients. Hypertonic solution also draws water into the intravascular compartment transiently.

body.black_box_warning: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis. QTc prolongation and torsades de pointes — ECG monitoring recommended, especially with IV use (off-label).
body.mechanism_of_action: Potent and selective dopamine D2 receptor antagonist (butyrophenone class). Very high D2 affinity → effective antipsychotic but high EPS risk. Minimal anticholinergic, antihistaminic, or antiadrenergic activity compared to phenothiazines.

Directly relaxes arteriolar smooth muscle via interference with calcium transport and release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum. Reduces systemic vascular resistance (afterload) without significant venodilation. Reflex tachycardia and RAAS activation occur compensatorily.

Inhibits the sodium-chloride cotransporter (NCC) in the distal convoluted tubule, reducing sodium and chloride reabsorption. Increases calcium reabsorption (opposite to loop diuretics). Produces a modest natriuresis (~5% of filtered sodium). Long-term BP reduction is primarily through decreased peripheral vascular resistance rather than volume depletion.

Identical to endogenous cortisol. Binds glucocorticoid receptors to regulate carbohydrate, protein, and lipid metabolism. At physiological doses, replaces deficient cortisol in primary (Addison disease) or secondary adrenal insufficiency. Glucocorticoid:mineralocorticoid ratio 1:1.
Binds intracellular glucocorticoid receptors in keratinocytes, suppressing phospholipase A2 and NF-kB pathways, reducing prostaglandin/leukotriene synthesis and inflammatory cell migration.

Converted to methylcobalamin and adenosylcobalamin, essential cofactors for methionine synthase (homocysteine to methionine) and methylmalonyl-CoA mutase. Required for DNA synthesis, neuronal myelin maintenance, and folate metabolism.

body.pregnancy_category: Category N (compatible — continue in SLE/RA during pregnancy per ACR)
body.mechanism_of_action: Accumulates in lysosomes, raising intravesicular pH and inhibiting antigen processing, TLR signalling, and cytokine production (TNF-α, IL-1, IL-6). In malaria, concentrates in parasite food vacuole and inhibits haem polymerisation.

Quaternary ammonium antimuscarinic that blocks muscarinic M3 receptors on smooth muscle of the GI and genitourinary tract, relieving spasm. Does not cross the blood-brain barrier — no central anticholinergic effects.

body.drug_class: Monoclonal antibody fragment (Fab) — direct thrombin inhibitor reversal agent
body.mechanism_of_action: Humanised monoclonal antibody fragment (Fab) that binds free and thrombin-bound dabigatran with 350-fold higher affinity than thrombin, forming a stable idarucizumab-dabigatran complex that is renally excreted. Rapidly and completely reverses the anticoagulant effect of dabigatran.

body.drug_class: Tyrosine kinase inhibitor (BCR-ABL, c-KIT, PDGFR inhibitor)
body.mechanism_of_action: Selectively inhibits BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase by competitively binding the ATP-binding site, preventing phosphorylation and downstream proliferative signaling. Also inhibits c-KIT and PDGFR receptor tyrosine kinases, blocking tumor cell proliferation and inducing apoptosis.

body.black_box_warning: Increased risk of serious infections (TB, invasive fungal, opportunistic); risk of lymphoma and other malignancies, particularly in pediatric patients.
body.mechanism_of_action: Chimeric IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds soluble and transmembrane TNF-alpha with high affinity, neutralizing its pro-inflammatory activity. Additionally induces macrophage IL-10 signalling, promoting anti-inflammatory polarization of intestinal macrophages — a key mechanism underlying therapeutic efficacy in IBD as demonstrated by Gearry et al. 2019.

Recombinant insulin analogue with substitution of proline at B28 with aspartic acid, preventing hexamer formation and allowing rapid absorption. Binds insulin receptors to promote glucose uptake into skeletal muscle and adipose tissue, and suppresses hepatic glucose output.

body.pregnancy_category: FDA Category B; use with caution — insulin requirements change significantly during pregnancy; human insulin preferred by some guidelines but insulin degludec considered acceptable
body.mechanism_of_action: Insulin degludec is a long-acting basal insulin analog that forms soluble multi-hexameric chains upon subcutaneous injection in the presence of zinc and phenol. As phenol disperses, the chains dissociate slowly into dihexamers and monomers, which are absorbed into the bloodstream. It binds to the insulin receptor (IR), activating the PI3K/Akt pathway to promote glucose uptake in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue, suppress hepatic glucose production, and inhibit lipolysis and ketogenesis. Its ultra-long duration results from the strong self-association mechanism and albumin binding via a C18 fatty diacid side chain, resulting in a half-life exceeding 25 hours and a flat, peakless pharmacodynamic profile over 42+ hours.

Recombinant human insulin analogue with substitution of asparagine at A21 with glycine and two arginines at B-chain C-terminus. Forms microprecipitates at physiological pH after SC injection, providing slow, peakless, prolonged release over ~24 hours. Binds insulin receptors to facilitate glucose uptake.
Binds insulin receptors on muscle, fat, and liver cells; stimulates glucose uptake, inhibits hepatic glucose output, and suppresses glucagon secretion
Competitive antagonist of muscarinic (M1-M3) acetylcholine receptors in bronchial smooth muscle, inhibiting vagally-mediated bronchoconstriction and mucus secretion.

Polynuclear iron(III)-hydroxide sucrose complex. After IV administration, iron dissociates from the sucrose complex in the reticuloendothelial system, enters the intracellular iron pool, and is incorporated into haemoglobin or stored as ferritin.
Inhibits fungal CYP51 (lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase), blocking ergosterol synthesis and disrupting fungal cell membrane integrity

body.black_box_warning: Severe and sometimes fatal hepatitis may occur, even after months of treatment. Monitor LFTs monthly; discontinue if transaminases exceed 3x ULN with symptoms or 5x ULN without symptoms.
body.mechanism_of_action: Inhibits mycolic acid synthesis by targeting InhA (enoyl-ACP reductase) after activation by catalase-peroxidase (KatG), disrupting the mycobacterial cell wall.

body.pregnancy_category: FDA Category C; TGA Category B2. Use only if benefit outweighs risk; no adequate well-controlled human studies available.
body.mechanism_of_action: Isosorbide dinitrate (ISDN) is an organic nitrate that undergoes enzymatic denitration in vascular smooth muscle to release nitric oxide (NO). NO activates soluble guanylate cyclase, increasing intracellular cyclic GMP (cGMP). Elevated cGMP activates protein kinase G, leading to dephosphorylation of myosin light chains and vascular smooth muscle relaxation. At low doses, venodilation predominates, reducing cardiac preload and ventricular wall stress. At higher doses, arterial dilation reduces afterload. Coronary vasodilation, particularly of large epicardial vessels, relieves vasospasm and improves perfusion to ischemic myocardium. The net effect is reduced myocardial oxygen demand and improved oxygen supply.

Converted to nitric oxide (NO) which activates guanylate cyclase, increasing cGMP in vascular smooth muscle. Primarily venodilation (reduces preload) at low doses; arteriolar dilation (reduces afterload) at higher doses. Coronary artery dilation improves myocardial oxygen supply.

body.drug_class: Hyperpolarisation-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channel blocker (If inhibitor)
body.mechanism_of_action: Selectively inhibits the If ("funny") current in the sinoatrial node, which controls spontaneous diastolic depolarisation. Reduces heart rate without affecting myocardial contractility, blood pressure, or intracardiac conduction.

Non-competitive antagonist of NMDA glutamate receptors producing dissociative anaesthesia with analgesia. Preserves airway reflexes and respiratory drive. Also interacts with opioid, monoaminergic, and muscarinic receptors.

body.drug_class: Anticonvulsant (functionalised amino acid, sodium channel blocker)
body.mechanism_of_action: Selectively enhances slow inactivation of voltage-gated sodium channels (unlike traditional AEDs that affect fast inactivation). This reduces pathological neuronal hyperexcitability without affecting normal physiological function. Also binds CRMP-2 (collapsin response mediator protein 2).

Synthetic disaccharide (galactose-fructose) not absorbed in the small intestine. Metabolised by colonic bacteria to lactic, acetic, and formic acids, which lower colonic pH. As laxative: osmotic effect draws water into the lumen. In hepatic encephalopathy: low pH converts ammonia (NH3) to non-absorbable ammonium (NH4+), trapping it in the colon for faecal excretion, and promotes growth of non-urease-producing bacteria.

body.black_box_warning: Serious skin rashes including Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN). Risk is highest in first 8 weeks and is increased by rapid dose escalation, concurrent valproate, and paediatric use.
body.mechanism_of_action: Blocks voltage-gated sodium channels, stabilising presynaptic neuronal membranes and inhibiting glutamate release. May also modulate calcium channels and HCN channels.

Selective agonist at the prostanoid FP receptor. Increases uveoscleral outflow of aqueous humour by remodelling the extracellular matrix of the ciliary muscle, reducing intraocular pressure by 25-35%.

body.black_box_warning: Embryo-fetal toxicity (Category X teratogen; REMS program required). Hematologic toxicity (severe neutropenia and thrombocytopenia). Deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism (VTE prophylaxis required in myeloma patients).
body.mechanism_of_action: Binds cereblon (CRBN), an E3 ubiquitin ligase component, leading to degradation of Ikaros (IKZF1) and Aiolos (IKZF3) transcription factors; inhibits tumor cell proliferation, enhances T-cell and NK-cell activity, inhibits angiogenesis, and modulates pro-inflammatory cytokines including TNF-α

Binds synaptic vesicle protein 2A (SV2A), modulating neurotransmitter release. Also inhibits N-type calcium channels and reverses inhibition of GABA- and glycine-gated currents induced by zinc and beta-carbolines.

Levodopa crosses the blood-brain barrier and is converted to dopamine by DOPA decarboxylase, replenishing striatal dopamine. Carbidopa inhibits peripheral DOPA decarboxylase, reducing peripheral conversion and side effects while increasing CNS levodopa availability.

body.black_box_warning: FDA Black Box Warning: Fluoroquinolones are associated with disabling and potentially irreversible serious adverse reactions including tendinitis/tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, and CNS effects. Also associated with aortic aneurysm/dissection. Reserve for conditions with no alternative treatment options.
body.mechanism_of_action: L-isomer of ofloxacin. Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV. Enhanced Gram-positive activity (especially S. pneumoniae) compared to ciprofloxacin — termed "respiratory fluoroquinolone".

body.pregnancy_category: Category A — safe; dose often needs increasing by 25-50% in pregnancy
body.mechanism_of_action: Synthetic form of endogenous thyroxine (T4). Converted peripherally to active triiodothyronine (T3) by deiodinases. T3 binds nuclear thyroid receptors, modulating gene transcription to regulate metabolic rate, growth, and development.

Inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding to the 23S ribosomal RNA of the 50S subunit, preventing formation of the 70S initiation complex. Bacteriostatic against enterococci and staphylococci; bactericidal against most streptococci.

body.black_box_warning: Liraglutide causes dose-dependent and treatment-duration-dependent thyroid C-cell tumors in both genders of rats and mice. It is unknown whether liraglutide causes thyroid C-cell tumors, including medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), in humans. Liraglutide is contraindicated in patients with a personal or family history of MTC and in patients with Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2).
body.pregnancy_category: FDA Category C (prior system); current FDA labeling advises discontinuation when pregnancy is recognized due to potential fetal harm observed in animal studies
body.mechanism_of_action: Liraglutide is a long-acting acylated analogue of human glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), sharing 97% amino acid sequence homology with endogenous GLP-1. It binds to and activates the GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R), a class B G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR), on pancreatic beta cells, stimulating adenylyl cyclase and increasing intracellular cyclic AMP (cAMP). This leads to glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppression of glucagon release from alpha cells, slowing of gastric emptying, and centrally mediated reduction in appetite via hypothalamic GLP-1R activation. The C-16 fatty acid chain attached via a glutamic acid linker allows albumin binding, which retards renal clearance and proteolytic degradation by dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4), conferring a plasma half-life suitable for once-daily dosing. Cardiovascular benefits include reduced inflammation, improved endothelial function, and modest reductions in blood pressure and heart rate.

body.black_box_warning: Drugs that act on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing foetus. Discontinue as soon as pregnancy is detected.
body.mechanism_of_action: Inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE), preventing conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II. Reduces aldosterone secretion, decreases peripheral vascular resistance, and increases bradykinin levels (responsible for cough side effect).

body.black_box_warning: Narrow therapeutic index. Lithium toxicity can be fatal. Serum lithium monitoring mandatory. Risk of nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, hypothyroidism, and renal impairment with chronic use. Teratogenic (Ebstein anomaly — cardiac).
body.mechanism_of_action: Exact mechanism unknown. Multiple proposed mechanisms: inhibition of inositol monophosphatase (depletes inositol → reduces PKC signalling), inhibition of glycogen synthase kinase-3 beta (GSK-3β) (neuroprotective), modulation of neurotransmitter release (serotonin, dopamine, glutamate), enhancement of GABA transmission, and effects on circadian rhythm gene expression.

Acts on mu-opioid receptors in the myenteric plexus of the gut wall, slowing peristalsis and increasing intestinal transit time. Increases anal sphincter tone. Does not cross the blood-brain barrier at therapeutic doses (P-glycoprotein substrate).

body.black_box_warning: Drugs that act on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing foetus. Discontinue as soon as pregnancy is detected.
body.mechanism_of_action: Selectively blocks the angiotensin II type 1 (AT1) receptor, preventing vasoconstriction, aldosterone release, and sympathetic activation. Does not inhibit ACE, so does not affect bradykinin — no cough. Active metabolite (EXP3174) is 10-40x more potent than parent compound.

body.pregnancy_category: Category C — considered low risk due to negligible systemic absorption
body.mechanism_of_action: High-molecular-weight polymer that is not absorbed or metabolised. Retains water in the bowel lumen by osmotic action, softening stool and increasing faecal volume to promote peristalsis.

body.pregnancy_category: Category D (if used >5-7 days may cause foetal bone abnormalities; short-term use in eclampsia is Category A)
body.mechanism_of_action: Essential cofactor for >300 enzymatic reactions. Blocks NMDA receptors (anticonvulsant effect in eclampsia). Stabilises cardiac cell membranes and suppresses early afterdepolarisations (anti-arrhythmic in torsades). Relaxes smooth muscle (bronchodilation, tocolysis). Corrects intracellular magnesium depletion that impairs K+ and Ca2+ homeostasis.

Freely filtered at the glomerulus but not reabsorbed — creates osmotic gradient in renal tubules promoting water excretion. In the brain, draws water from cerebral tissue across an intact BBB, reducing intracranial pressure.

Uncompetitive, low-affinity voltage-dependent antagonist of NMDA-type glutamate receptors; blocks excessive calcium influx caused by pathological glutamate activity while preserving physiological NMDA receptor function; reduces excitotoxicity implicated in Alzheimer's neurodegeneration

Humanized IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody that binds IL-5 with high affinity, blocking IL-5 from binding to its receptor on eosinophils, thereby reducing eosinophil production, maturation, recruitment, and survival

Binds to PBPs (PBP2 and PBP3) and inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis. Ultra-broad spectrum — stable against most beta-lactamases including ESBLs and AmpC. Does NOT require co-administration with cilastatin (unlike imipenem).

body.pregnancy_category: Category B: Generally considered safe during pregnancy; limited human data suggest no increased risk of major congenital malformations. Use if clearly indicated. Avoid high-dose therapy near term due to theoretical risk of neonatal renal impairment and premature closure of ductus arteriosus.
body.mechanism_of_action: Mesalazine (5-aminosalicylic acid, 5-ASA) exerts its anti-inflammatory effects locally within the gastrointestinal mucosa through multiple mechanisms: (1) Inhibition of nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) signaling, reducing pro-inflammatory cytokine production (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α); (2) Inhibition of cyclooxygenase (COX) and 5-lipoxygenase pathways, reducing prostaglandin E2 and leukotriene B4 synthesis; (3) Activation of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-gamma (PPAR-γ), promoting anti-inflammatory gene expression; (4) Scavenging of reactive oxygen species (ROS) within the intestinal mucosa; (5) Inhibition of leucocyte chemotaxis and adhesion molecule expression; (6) Modulation of the gut microbiome. The predominant action is topical rather than systemic, requiring direct mucosal contact for therapeutic efficacy.
Decreases hepatic glucose production, increases insulin sensitivity in peripheral tissues (skeletal muscle), reduces intestinal absorption of glucose. Activates AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK).

body.black_box_warning: Hepatotoxicity, pulmonary toxicity, bone marrow suppression, teratogenicity, malignant lymphomas, serious infections. Use only by physicians experienced in antimetabolite therapy.
body.mechanism_of_action: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR), blocking conversion of dihydrofolate to tetrahydrofolate. At low doses used in rheumatology, anti-inflammatory effects are mediated primarily through adenosine release and inhibition of polyamine synthesis.

body.pregnancy_category: Category B — longest safety record in pregnancy hypertension
body.mechanism_of_action: Converted to alpha-methylnoradrenaline in the CNS, which stimulates alpha-2 adrenergic receptors in the brainstem vasomotor centre, reducing sympathetic outflow and peripheral vascular resistance.

Antagonises dopamine D2 receptors in the CTZ (antiemetic) and in the upper GI tract (prokinetic). Also acts as a 5-HT4 agonist, enhancing acetylcholine release in the myenteric plexus, increasing gastric motility and accelerating gastric emptying. Weak 5-HT3 antagonist activity at high doses.

Selectively blocks beta-1 adrenergic receptors in the heart, reducing heart rate, myocardial contractility, and AV conduction. Decreases renin release from the kidney. At higher doses, selectivity diminishes and beta-2 blockade may occur.

Prodrug reduced intracellularly by anaerobic organisms to reactive nitro radical intermediates that damage DNA, inhibiting nucleic acid synthesis. Selectively toxic to anaerobes and certain protozoa. Bactericidal.
Inhibits 1,3-β-D-glucan synthase, disrupting fungal cell wall synthesis; fungicidal against Candida, fungistatic against Aspergillus
Enhances GABA-A receptor-mediated chloride conductance by binding the benzodiazepine site, producing anxiolysis, sedation, amnesia, and anticonvulsant effects.

Selectively inhibits phosphodiesterase-3 in cardiac and vascular smooth muscle, increasing intracellular cAMP. In the heart this enhances contractility (inotropy) and lusitropy; in blood vessels it causes vasodilation, reducing afterload and preload.

body.black_box_warning: Suicidality in young adults.
body.mechanism_of_action: Antagonist at presynaptic alpha-2 adrenergic autoreceptors and heteroreceptors (enhances noradrenaline and serotonin release). Blocks 5-HT2A, 5-HT2C, 5-HT3 receptors (anxiolytic, anti-emetic, avoids sexual dysfunction). Potent histamine H1 antagonist (sedation, weight gain). No serotonin reuptake inhibition.

body.black_box_warning: FDA boxed warning (2020): Serious neuropsychiatric events including suicidal thoughts and actions. Reserve for patients who are inadequately controlled on or intolerant of other therapies.
body.mechanism_of_action: Selective competitive antagonist of the cysteinyl leukotriene receptor CysLT1. Blocks leukotriene D4 (LTD4) binding, reducing bronchoconstriction, mucus secretion, airway oedema, and eosinophil recruitment.
Reversibly binds to bacterial isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase, preventing incorporation of isoleucine into bacterial proteins. This unique mechanism means no cross-resistance with other antibiotic classes.

body.black_box_warning: Teratogenicity (pregnancy category D/X — REMS programme). Increased risk of infection and lymphoma. Only prescribed by physicians experienced in immunosuppressive therapy.
body.mechanism_of_action: Prodrug hydrolysed to mycophenolic acid (MPA), which reversibly inhibits inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase (IMPDH), selectively blocking de novo purine synthesis in T and B lymphocytes (which lack the salvage pathway). Results in selective lymphocyte suppression.

body.drug_class: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) — non-selective COX inhibitor
body.pregnancy_category: Category C (Category D in third trimester — risk of premature closure of ductus arteriosus)
body.mechanism_of_action: Non-selectively inhibits cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1) and cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), reducing prostaglandin E2 and prostacyclin synthesis. This decreases inflammation, pain, and fever. COX-1 inhibition accounts for GI and platelet side effects.

Inhibits L-type calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle, producing potent peripheral and coronary vasodilation. Reduces afterload and myocardial oxygen demand. More potent vasodilator than amlodipine but shorter acting.

body.pregnancy_category: Category B (avoid at term — risk of neonatal haemolytic anaemia)
body.mechanism_of_action: Reduced by bacterial flavoproteins to reactive intermediates that damage DNA, RNA, proteins, and cell wall synthesis. Multiple mechanisms make resistance uncommon. Bactericidal at urinary concentrations.

Releases nitric oxide (NO) which activates guanylyl cyclase, increasing cGMP in vascular smooth muscle. Predominantly venodilator at low doses (reducing preload); arterial dilation occurs at higher doses (reducing afterload).

Fully human IgG4 monoclonal antibody that binds to PD-1 receptor on T-cells, blocking interaction with PD-L1 and PD-L2 ligands on tumor cells, thereby restoring anti-tumor T-cell immune activity and promoting tumor cell killing

body.drug_class: Endogenous catecholamine — predominantly alpha-1 agonist with beta-1 activity
body.mechanism_of_action: Potent alpha-1 agonist (vasoconstriction, increases SVR and MAP) with moderate beta-1 activity (inotropy). Minimal beta-2 activity, so no vasodilation or bronchodilation. Net effect: increased MAP with preserved or slightly increased cardiac output.

Synthetic octapeptide analogue of somatostatin. Binds somatostatin receptors (primarily SSTR2 and SSTR5), inhibiting secretion of growth hormone, insulin, glucagon, gastrin, VIP, and serotonin. Reduces splanchnic blood flow and portal pressure. Inhibits pancreatic and GI secretions.

body.black_box_warning: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis — not approved for this indication. Olanzapine long-acting injection (Zyprexa Relprevv): post-injection delirium/sedation syndrome (PDSS) — requires 3-hour observation period.
body.mechanism_of_action: Multi-receptor antagonist: dopamine D1-D4 (especially D2), serotonin 5-HT2A/2C, muscarinic M1-M5, histamine H1, and alpha-1 adrenergic receptors. High 5-HT2A/D2 ratio (atypical antipsychotic profile). 5-HT2C and H1 blockade primarily responsible for metabolic side effects.

body.black_box_warning: Anaphylaxis has been reported after administration; observe patients for an appropriate period after injection and be prepared to manage anaphylaxis.
body.mechanism_of_action: Recombinant humanized monoclonal IgG1 antibody that selectively binds free serum IgE, preventing IgE from binding to high-affinity FcεRI receptors on mast cells and basophils, thereby reducing allergic inflammatory cascade; unlike UB-221, omalizumab does not mediate CD23-dependent IgE downregulation.

Irreversibly inhibits the gastric H+/K+ ATPase (proton pump) on the apical surface of parietal cells. Prodrug that is acid-activated in the secretory canaliculus, forming a sulphenamide that binds covalently to cysteine residues on the pump. Reduces basal and stimulated gastric acid secretion by >90%.

body.pregnancy_category: Category B (widely used off-label in hyperemesis; some concern for cleft palate at very low absolute risk)
body.mechanism_of_action: Selective antagonist of serotonin 5-HT3 receptors, both peripherally on vagal afferents in the GI tract and centrally in the chemoreceptor trigger zone (CTZ) and nucleus tractus solitarius. Blocks serotonin-mediated emetic signals triggered by chemotherapy, radiation, surgery, and other stimuli.
Prodrug hydrolysed to oseltamivir carboxylate, which selectively inhibits influenza virus neuraminidase. Prevents release of newly formed virions from infected cells, limiting viral spread.

body.black_box_warning: Risk of addiction, abuse, misuse, life-threatening respiratory depression, accidental ingestion (especially children), neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome, and fatal interaction with benzodiazepines/CNS depressants.
body.pregnancy_category: Category C (Category D if prolonged use or high doses at term)
body.mechanism_of_action: Full agonist at mu-opioid receptors in the CNS and peripheral tissues. Activates inhibitory G-proteins, reducing cAMP, opening potassium channels, and closing calcium channels, resulting in decreased neuronal excitability and pain signal transmission.

body.pregnancy_category: Safe in pregnancy — use to correct maternal hypoxaemia
body.mechanism_of_action: Increases alveolar and arterial partial pressure of oxygen (PaO2), improving oxygen delivery to tissues. Corrects hypoxaemia by increasing the fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) above 21% (room air).

Irreversibly inhibits gastric H+/K+ ATPase proton pump. Activated in the acidic environment of parietal cell canaliculus. Binds cysteine 813 and 822 residues specifically, providing sustained acid suppression.
Non-absorbed, cation-exchange polymer that binds potassium in the distal colon in exchange for calcium, increasing fecal potassium excretion and lowering serum potassium levels

body.black_box_warning: Immune-mediated adverse reactions, including fatal events, may occur in any organ system. Early identification and management with corticosteroids is critical.
body.mechanism_of_action: Humanized IgG4 monoclonal antibody that binds PD-1 receptor on T-cells, blocking its interaction with PD-L1 and PD-L2 ligands, thereby restoring anti-tumor T-cell immune activity and enhancing immune-mediated tumor cell killing.

body.black_box_warning: Serious psychiatric and behavioral reactions including aggression, hostility, irritability, anger, and homicidal ideation reported; monitor for behavioral changes
body.mechanism_of_action: Selective, non-competitive AMPA (alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid) glutamate receptor antagonist; reduces neuronal excitation by blocking glutamate-mediated synaptic transmission
Disrupts sodium channel function in arthropod nerve cell membranes, causing delayed repolarisation, paralysis, and death of the parasite. Acts on both adult mites and eggs (ovicidal).

Pure alpha-1 adrenergic agonist causing peripheral arteriolar vasoconstriction, increasing systemic vascular resistance and blood pressure. No direct beta-1 or beta-2 activity. Reflex bradycardia may occur due to baroreceptor activation.

body.black_box_warning: IV phenytoin: cardiovascular risk — severe hypotension and cardiac arrhythmias with rapid IV administration. Must not exceed 50 mg/min in adults (25 mg/min in elderly). Requires cardiac monitoring and BP during infusion. Purple glove syndrome with peripheral IV extravasation.
body.mechanism_of_action: Stabilises voltage-gated sodium channels in their inactivated state, prolonging the refractory period. Reduces sustained high-frequency repetitive firing of action potentials. Does not affect normal low-frequency firing.

Essential cofactor for hepatic gamma-carboxylation of clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X (and proteins C and S). Reverses warfarin by restoring the vitamin K epoxide cycle, enabling synthesis of functional coagulation factors.

body.black_box_warning: Congestive Heart Failure: May cause or exacerbate CHF. Not recommended in symptomatic heart failure. Contraindicated in NYHA Class III-IV heart failure.
body.mechanism_of_action: Selective agonist of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPAR-γ); enhances insulin sensitivity in adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, and liver; reduces hepatic glucose output and increases glucose uptake

Piperacillin inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to PBPs. Tazobactam irreversibly inhibits many class A and some class C beta-lactamases, extending coverage to beta-lactamase-producing organisms.
Inhibits CYP51A1 (lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase), blocking ergosterol synthesis and disrupting fungal cell membrane integrity

Provides exogenous potassium ions essential for maintaining resting membrane potential, cardiac conduction, nerve impulse transmission, and muscle contraction. Chloride component helps correct concurrent metabolic alkalosis (common with diuretic-induced hypokalaemia).

Selective non-ergot dopamine agonist with high affinity for D2/D3 receptors in striatum and substantia nigra; reduces motor symptoms in Parkinson's disease and modulates sensory pathways in restless legs syndrome

body.black_box_warning: Prasugrel can cause significant, sometimes fatal, bleeding. Do not use in patients with active pathological bleeding or a history of transient ischemic attack (TIA) or stroke. In patients ≥75 years of age, prasugrel is generally not recommended due to increased risk of fatal and intracranial bleeding and uncertain benefit, except in high-risk situations (diabetes mellitus or history of prior MI) where its effect appears to be greater and its use may be considered. Do not start prasugrel in patients likely to undergo urgent coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG); discontinue at least 7 days prior to any surgery. Additional risk factors for bleeding include body weight <60 kg, propensity to bleed, and concomitant use of medications that increase bleeding risk.
body.pregnancy_category: B (FDA legacy classification) — Animal studies have not demonstrated fetal harm; no adequate well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Use only if clearly needed and benefit outweighs risk.
body.mechanism_of_action: Prasugrel is a thienopyridine prodrug that requires hepatic biotransformation to an active thiol metabolite. The active metabolite irreversibly binds to the P2Y12 ADP receptor on platelet surfaces, thereby inhibiting ADP-mediated platelet activation and aggregation. Because prasugrel binds irreversibly, the antiplatelet effect persists for the lifetime of the affected platelet (7–10 days). Compared to clopidogrel, prasugrel achieves faster onset, higher levels of platelet inhibition, and less interpatient variability due to more efficient conversion to its active metabolite with less dependence on CYP2C19 polymorphisms.

body.pregnancy_category: Category C (Category D in first trimester — cleft palate risk)
body.mechanism_of_action: Binds intracellular glucocorticoid receptors, translocates to nucleus, and modulates gene transcription. Suppresses inflammatory cascade by inhibiting NF-κB and AP-1, reducing prostaglandins, leukotrienes, and pro-inflammatory cytokines. Glucocorticoid:mineralocorticoid potency ratio 4:1 (relative to hydrocortisone).
Blocks dopamine D2 receptors in the chemoreceptor trigger zone and vestibular pathways. Also has weak anticholinergic and antihistaminic activity contributing to antiemetic and anti-vertigo effects.

body.black_box_warning: Propofol infusion syndrome (PRIS): fatal if infusion >4 mg/kg/h for >48 h — monitor lactate, CK, and triglycerides.
body.mechanism_of_action: Potentiates GABA-A receptor activity and inhibits NMDA glutamate receptors, producing rapid-onset sedation and amnesia without analgesic properties.

Non-selective beta-blocker (beta-1 and beta-2). Migraine prophylaxis mechanism not fully understood: thought to involve central beta-receptor blockade reducing neuronal excitability, inhibition of noradrenaline release, modulation of serotonergic neurotransmission, and possible effects on nitric oxide synthesis.

body.black_box_warning: Severe hepatotoxicity including fulminant hepatic failure and death — reserve for patients intolerant of methimazole or in the first trimester of pregnancy
body.pregnancy_category: Category D — preferred over methimazole in 1st trimester (lower teratogenic risk)
body.mechanism_of_action: Inhibits thyroid peroxidase, blocking iodine organification and coupling of iodotyrosines. Also inhibits peripheral conversion of T4 to T3.

Strongly basic protein derived from fish sperm that forms a stable, inactive complex with the strongly acidic heparin molecule, neutralising its anticoagulant activity. Less effective against low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) as it only partially neutralises anti-Xa activity.
Prodrug converted to pyrazinoic acid by mycobacterial pyrazinamidase (PncA). Disrupts membrane energetics and inhibits fatty acid synthase I in acidic environments (e.g. within macrophages).

body.black_box_warning: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis. Suicidality in young adults when used for depression.
body.mechanism_of_action: Antagonist at dopamine D2 (loosely bound — "fast-off"), serotonin 5-HT2A, histamine H1, and alpha-1 adrenergic receptors. Active metabolite norquetiapine is a potent noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor (NRI) and 5-HT2C antagonist — contributes to antidepressant effect. Transiently occupies D2 receptors — lower EPS risk.

body.black_box_warning: Drugs that act on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing foetus. Discontinue as soon as pregnancy is detected.
body.mechanism_of_action: Prodrug hydrolysed in the liver to ramiprilat, a potent ACE inhibitor. Has high tissue ACE affinity — provides sustained RAAS suppression with once-daily dosing. Reduces cardiovascular events beyond blood pressure lowering (pleiotropic effects).

body.black_box_warning: WITHDRAWN from most markets (2020) due to unacceptable levels of NDMA (N-nitrosodimethylamine), a probable carcinogen. Included here for historical reference and board examination preparation only. Use famotidine as alternative.
body.mechanism_of_action: Competitively and reversibly blocks histamine H2 receptors on gastric parietal cells, reducing basal and meal-stimulated gastric acid secretion by ~70%.

Inhibits the late inward sodium current (late INa) in cardiac myocytes, reducing intracellular sodium and calcium overload, thereby decreasing diastolic wall tension and myocardial oxygen demand without significantly affecting heart rate or blood pressure
Closes ATP-sensitive potassium channels on pancreatic beta-cell membranes, causing depolarization and calcium influx, stimulating glucose-dependent insulin secretion

body.black_box_warning: Severe hepatotoxicity including fatalities reported, especially with concurrent hepatotoxic drugs or pre-existing liver disease.
body.mechanism_of_action: Inhibits bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase by binding to the beta subunit, blocking RNA transcription. Bactericidal with excellent intracellular activity — kills semi-dormant bacilli within macrophages (crucial for TB sterilisation).

body.black_box_warning: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis; not approved for this use
body.mechanism_of_action: Antagonist at dopamine D2 receptors and serotonin 5-HT2A receptors; also blocks alpha-1 adrenergic, H1 histamine, and alpha-2 adrenergic receptors. D2 antagonism reduces positive psychotic symptoms; 5-HT2A antagonism modulates dopamine release in prefrontal cortex improving negative symptoms and reducing EPS risk

body.black_box_warning: Fatal infusion reactions, severe mucocutaneous reactions (SJS/TEN), progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), and hepatitis B virus reactivation with fulminant hepatitis reported.
body.mechanism_of_action: Chimeric anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody that binds CD20 on pre-B and mature B lymphocytes, causing B-cell depletion via complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC), antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC), and apoptosis.
Directly and selectively inhibits free and clot-bound Factor Xa, interrupting the intrinsic and extrinsic coagulation pathways. Does not require antithrombin for activity.
Competitive antagonist at nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, preventing depolarisation and producing skeletal muscle paralysis.

body.black_box_warning: Psychiatric events including suicidal ideation, depression, and insomnia have been reported; weigh risks and benefits in patients with history of depression or suicidal thoughts
body.mechanism_of_action: Selective inhibitor of phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4), reducing breakdown of cAMP in inflammatory cells (neutrophils, macrophages, T-cells), thereby decreasing cytokine release and airway inflammation in COPD
Competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase. More hydrophilic and hepato-selective than atorvastatin. Upregulates hepatic LDL receptor expression, increasing LDL-C clearance.

body.black_box_warning: Drugs that act on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing foetus. Discontinue as soon as pregnancy is detected.
body.mechanism_of_action: Dual mechanism: sacubitril is a prodrug of sacubitrilat (LBQ657), which inhibits neprilysin, increasing levels of natriuretic peptides (ANP, BNP, CNP), bradykinin, and adrenomedullin — promoting vasodilation, natriuresis, and anti-fibrotic effects. Valsartan blocks AT1 receptors. The combination provides synergistic neurohormonal modulation.
